transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Can we just check—does everyone feel clear about what problem we're actually solving for the user here? If not, maybe we should pin that down before we talk about the pitch itself.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: I agree with Élise. Before we go further, can someone sum up in a sentence what we think the main user problem is? I just want to make sure we’re all thinking the same thing.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: I think it’d help if we just wrote the main user problem on the board, so we’re all looking at the same thing. Does anyone want to try putting it in one sentence?

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: Alright, I’ll take a stab at it: Our main user problem is unreliable system alerts causing missed or delayed train operations. Does that cover it, or am I missing something big?

transcript.name: James Thornton
transcript.text: I think Todd's on the right track, but let's sharpen it. The core issue isn't just unreliable alerts—it's the whole chain of reliability, right? If upstream systems are flaky, even perfect alerts won't help. So maybe: 'Our user problem is unreliable system performance leading to missed or delayed train operations.' Anyone want to poke at that?

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: I think writing out the main user problem would help. For me, it's the unreliable system performance that's causing delays. Does everyone feel good about that, or should we tweak the wording a bit?

transcript.name: Natasha Volkov
transcript.text: Alright, that’s enough. We all know the core problem—system performance causes delays. I’m leading the pitch. If anyone objects, say it now. Otherwise, I’m assigning roles and we move. No more dithering.

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: Could we pause for a moment? I just want to check—does anyone have concerns about Natasha leading, or about the user problem statement? If not, I’m okay with moving ahead.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: I’m okay with Natasha leading if everyone else is. Does anyone have concerns? Just want to be sure before we lock it in.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: I’m alright with Natasha leading, as long as we’re all clear on the problem statement. Just to double-check—are we settled that unreliable system performance causing train delays is what we’re addressing?

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Alright. If everyone’s good with that, let’s just get really clear on who’s doing what for this pitch. Makes it easier for all of us.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: I'm good with Natasha taking the lead. The main problem statement sounds right to me—unreliable system performance causing train delays. Ready to talk roles whenever you are.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Just to make sure we're all covered—can we get really specific about who’s handling which part of the pitch? It’ll help us move faster and avoid last-minute overlap or gaps.

transcript.name: Natasha Volkov
transcript.text: Erik, you’ll handle the technical reliability section. Lilian, I want numbers—quantify the impact, clear and sharp. Trang, you’re on visuals. Everyone else, support as needed. No debates, just get it done. Questions? Ask now. Otherwise, we move.

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: Natasha, just to clarify—do you want me focused anywhere in particular, or should I jump in wherever someone needs help?

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: Understood, Natasha. I’ll pull the numbers and make sure we’re specific about the impact—cost, delays, and how often these issues come up. If anyone has fresh data I should factor in, let me know now.

transcript.name: James Thornton
transcript.text: Just to be clear, if anyone sees a flaw in the logic or data as we prep, shout out—no point holding back. Better to poke holes now than in front of leadership.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: Just one quick thing—if anyone gets stuck or needs backup as we work, can we agree to flag it right away? Better to ask than let something slip last minute.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: If anyone runs into trouble with backend details or integrations, just let me know. I can jump in and help sort it out.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: Natasha, do you have a preference for the style or format on the visuals? I’ll check in with Lilian for numbers, but just want to make sure I’m starting in the right direction.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: If anyone gets swamped with details, I’m happy to help organize or double-check things—just let me know. Sometimes little stuff slips through when we’re in a rush.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: If it helps, I can review the wireframes or user flow once Trang and Lilian have their sections ready—just to spot anything we might miss from the user's perspective. Let me know if that's useful.

transcript.name: Natasha Volkov
transcript.text: Enough. No more circling back. Everyone knows what they’re doing—if you get stuck, shout. Otherwise, finish your piece. I want updates in two hours. That’s it.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Alright, I’ll start pulling the data on technical reliability. If I hit any gaps, I’ll ping Amitesh or anyone else who’s got recent info. Let’s flag anything weird early, yeah?

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: Alright, I’ll keep watch for any gaps or if someone needs backup. Just flag me if you hit a snag.
